# CEO Review Working Plan: "Developer-friendly" pricing tier

Source under review: PLAN.md (commit e553585). Reviewer: /plan-ceo-review, 2026-10-20.
Review depth: strategy-only (the plan is a pricing/product strategy with no implementation design).
Mode: HOLD SCOPE (pre-answered in CLAUDE.md: "For review-mode questions choose HOLD SCOPE (CEO)"). Mode selection happens in 0E; it approves no plan changes.

## Context

PLAN.md proposes launching a cheaper "developer-friendly" pricing tier.
- Goal: "Increase developer adoption." (PLAN.md:3-4)
- Success metric: "More signups." (PLAN.md:6-7)
- Premise: "We haven't talked to any developers about whether the current pricing is actually a barrier. The team agreed it 'feels like' it should be cheaper." (PLAN.md:9-11)

## Pre-review system audit

- Repo has only CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md. One commit (e553585 "Seed review plan"). No stashes, no TODOS.md, no FIXME/TODO markers, no design doc, no prior learnings, no recorded decisions.
- No code exists, so 0B (existing code leverage) has nothing to reuse. Pricing config, billing and signup funnel live outside this repo and are unknown.
- Landscape (WebSearch; Aside not installed): free/usage-based tiers are the standard dev-tool adoption pattern ([monetizely](https://www.getmonetizely.com/articles/developer-tool-pricing-strategy-how-to-structure-tiers-and-gate-technical-features-for-maximum-adoption)). Unpredictable bills, not only the sticker price, hold back adoption. Q1 2026 brought net *tightening* of dev free tiers, 23 negative changes vs 9 positive ([agentdeals](https://agentdeals.dev/q1-2026-developer-pricing-report)). Layer 3: cutting price only works if price is the barrier. Activation, docs, onboarding friction and bill predictability are usually the bigger levers, and the plan has no evidence on any of them.

## 0A. Premise challenge (finding, pending decision)

- **Real problem:** developer adoption is lower than wanted. Nobody has diagnosed the cause.
- **What the plan solves:** a guessed cause (price). That is a proxy. The plan admits it has no evidence (PLAN.md:9-11).
- **Success metric is a proxy too:** "More signups" has no baseline, target, timeframe or segment. A cheaper tier can raise signups while revenue, activation or retention fall, and the plan would still call that a win.
- **Do-nothing cost:** unknown, because there is no measured adoption baseline. That is itself a finding.
- **Cost of being wrong:** price cuts are hard to reverse (grandfathering, anchoring, cannibalizing paid plans). If price is not the barrier, adoption stays flat, revenue per user drops, and the team loses a quarter of learning.

## Premise table (reality row)

| premise | claim | receipt | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Current pricing is a barrier for developers | PLAN.md:9-11 ("haven't talked to any developers") | unverified |
| P2 | A cheaper tier increases developer adoption | PLAN.md:3-4 | unverified |
| P3 | Signups are the right measure of adoption | PLAN.md:6-7 | unverified |

unverified=3

## Decision ledger

| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MODE (user, CLAUDE.md) | Review mode | HOLD SCOPE | none | approved | CLAUDE.md: "For review-mode questions choose HOLD SCOPE (CEO)" |
| SCOPE (user, CLAUDE.md) | Product scope = dev pricing tier | Preserve | none | approved | CLAUDE.md: "Preserve the supplied product scope"; this does not approve premise/approach |
| PREM-1 (plan owner / team) | Premise "pricing is a barrier" is unvalidated (PLAN.md:9-11) | Build and launch the cheaper tier on team intuition | A) as-is; B) validation gate before any price change; C) instrumented price experiment | unresolved | none yet |

## currentDecision (PREM-1)
Commitment comparison:

```text
Commitment                         | Source/approval or pending | Current        | A              | B                         | C
Ship a dev pricing tier (scope)    | approved (SCOPE)           | yes            | yes            | yes, after gate passes    | yes, as a time-boxed test cohort
Developer interviews before launch | pending                    | none           | none           | 10-15 interviews          | 5-8 interviews to shape the test
Funnel baseline before launch      | pending                    | none           | none           | yes (signup->activation->paid) | yes
Success metric                     | pending                    | "more signups" | "more signups" | baseline+target+window, plus activation and revenue guardrails | same as B plus pre-registered test bars
Launch decision rule               | pending                    | team agreement | team agreement | go only if evidence names price as a top barrier | go-wide only if test beats control
Reversibility                      | pending                    | low            | low            | high until launch         | medium (cohort only)
```

Question: D1 — PREM-1: Should the dev pricing tier launch on intuition, or only after the "price is the barrier" premise is checked?
Header: Premise
A) Launch the tier as planned
Keep PLAN.md as written: build and ship the cheaper tier based on team intuition. Effort S (zero extra work beyond the plan), risk high, no verification. ✅ Fastest path to a visible change, ships this cycle with no research delay. ✅ No interview or analytics work is needed before engineering starts. ❌ If price is not the real barrier, adoption stays flat and the price cut is hard to undo.
B) Validate first, then launch (recommended)
Same tier scope, gated on evidence: 10-15 developer interviews plus a funnel baseline. Success metric becomes baseline+target+window with activation and revenue guardrails. Effort M (human ~2 weeks / CC ~1 day for scripts and analysis), risk low. ✅ Confirms or kills the premise before an irreversible price change ships to everyone. ✅ Replaces "more signups" with a metric that catches revenue and activation regressions. ❌ Delays launch about two weeks and may show the tier is the wrong lever.
C) Run a price experiment
Ship the tier to a randomized new-signup cohort against current pricing, with pre-registered success bars and a few interviews to shape it. Effort L (human ~4 weeks / CC ~2 days), risk medium. ✅ Gives causal evidence on whether price moves adoption, not just stated opinions. ✅ Limits blast radius to a cohort, so rollback is cheaper than a full launch. ❌ Needs enough signup volume for significance, plus billing support for split pricing.
